description: Probe queries used to inspect retrieval quality. Each in_corpus entry captures the Day 2 retrieval observation, the Day 3 end-to-end finding (after the LLM synthesised over retrieved chunks), and a failure_mode tag pointing at the technique that would fix the remaining real gap. The out_of_corpus entries probe whether the citation-aware prompt successfully refuses to answer when grounding is absent.

in_corpus.notes: Single-entity definitional query. Top 3 all from the Gandalf article. Baseline retrieval handles this cleanly.
in_corpus.day_3_finding: Still good end-to-end. Top-4 all from Gandalf article. Answer cites [1][2][3] correctly, covers Istari/Olórin/Mithrandir/appearance/major deeds without leaking outside knowledge.

in_corpus.notes: Day 2 verdict 'partial / recall-not-ranking'. Bard's own article never made the candidate set; retrieval pulled Smaug-centric chunks.
in_corpus.day_3_finding: Falsified the Day 2 prognosis. Retrieval still pulls Smaug-centric chunks (Dragons in ME, Thorin II, Smaug, ME peoples — no Bard article), but every one of them mentions Bard, and Claude synthesised a complete answer (Bard / Black Arrow / Lake-town / thrush / Bilbo's discovery) with correct inline citations. HyDE / query decomposition on Day 8 is now a NICE-TO-HAVE, not the load-bearing fix. Reclassify: synthesis recovered the multi-hop.

in_corpus.query: What rings did the Dwarves get?
in_corpus.notes: Both sources' Dwarves articles surfaced. Cross-source consensus on factual queries is a positive signal.
in_corpus.day_3_finding: Still good. Both sources' Dwarves articles + WP Dwarves-in-Middle-earth surfaced. Answer correctly distinguishes the Dwarven outcome (greed, not wraithdom) from the Men/Nazgûl outcome and traces Durin III -> Thrór -> Thráin II line. Cross-source consensus held.

in_corpus.query: Tell me about the Battle of Five Armies
in_corpus.notes: Day 2 verdict 'good-with-noise / chunk-cleaning'. The retrieved chunk leads with Fandom maintenance template text ('The descriptive majority of this article's text is unsourced...').
in_corpus.day_3_finding: Template noise was invisible in the final answer — Claude ignored the maintenance text and gave a clean account of the battle (allies, Bolg/Gundabad, Thorin/Fíli/Kíli wounded, Beorn slays Bolg, Bilbo knocked out). Day 2.5 chunk cleanup is genuinely lower priority than Day 2 implied. Keep it as nice-to-have, not blocking.

in_corpus.notes: Day 2 verdict 'partial / reranking'. Edith Tolkien's gravestone chunk surfaced at #3 and looked like wrong-context noise that a cross-encoder would demote.
in_corpus.day_3_finding: Falsified the 'reranking is the fix' diagnosis. Claude integrated the Edith Tolkien grave chunk as a closing paragraph ('Tolkien identified himself and his wife Edith with these characters, having BEREN inscribed on his own grave marker and LUTHIEN on hers'). The chunk wasn't wrong-context — it was real biographical context the LLM used appropriately. Demoting it with a reranker would have made the answer worse, not better.

in_corpus.notes: All three results from Wikipedia's Mithril article. Definitional 'what is X?' queries naturally favor Wikipedia's encyclopedic prose over Fandom's narrative style.
in_corpus.day_3_finding: Still good and still Wikipedia-dominated (4/4 chunks from WP Mithril). Source-style observation from Day 2 confirmed: encyclopedic prose wins definitional queries. Etymology (mith + ril) and Hobbit/FotR quotes both made it into the answer.

in_corpus.notes: Day 2 verdict 'partial / hybrid-search'. Bombadil's own dedicated article was not the top hit.
in_corpus.day_3_finding: The one case the LLM CANNOT compensate for, and the most diagnostically useful query in the set. Retrieval still surfaces Middle-earth peoples / Adventures of Tom Bombadil / Barrow-wight — Bombadil's own page never enters the candidate set. Answer is good because the candidate chunks happen to summarise him, but Goldberry / Withywindle / Old Forest specifics are absent. This is the clean example of the candidate-set-miss class of failure: hybrid BM25 + dense retrieval (Day 6) is the load-bearing fix. Reranking won't help; synthesis can't compensate. Re-run this exact query immediately after Day 6 to confirm hybrid lifts the right document into top-k.

out_of_corpus.expected_behavior: Refuse: 'context does not contain information about ...'
out_of_corpus.notes: Verifies the system prompt's 'answer only from context' constraint holds for a question that sounds Tolkien-flavoured but has no in-corpus answer.

out_of_corpus.query: What did Frodo have for breakfast on the third Tuesday of Halimath?
out_of_corpus.expected_behavior: Refuse: specific fabricated detail with no source.
out_of_corpus.notes: Probes whether Claude confabulates plausible-sounding specifics when the corpus is silent. Halimath is a real Shire-reckoning month so the question reads grounded but is unanswerable.

out_of_corpus.query: How does the One Ring compare to the rings in Wagner's Der Ring des Nibelungen?
out_of_corpus.expected_behavior: Refuse or use Outside context: prefix. Tolkien wikis discuss the One Ring extensively but not the Wagner comparison.
out_of_corpus.notes: Tests the gap between in-corpus topic (One Ring) and out-of-corpus claim (Wagner comparison). Easiest failure mode for an LLM: half the question has rich grounding, half doesn't.
